matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: First compute the decimal values of both sides of the equation (including any operators) to find the numeric imbalance, then look for a single‑stick move that changes a numeral or operator by exactly that amount.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation is false, compute the difference between the two sides before deciding which stick to move.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick arbitrarily without first computing the numeric difference, resulting in an equation that remains false.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the side that must increase contains a V and the numeric imbalance is exactly +5, reposition one of the V’s diagonal sticks so that the V becomes an X, increasing its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is +5 and a V is present on the side that needs to increase.
matchstick.example: Attempting to add a vertical stick to a V to make an X, which changes orientation and is illegal.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral that already has at least one I to another numeral that can accept an extra I, adjusting the values by ±1 on each side.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance can be resolved by moving a single I (e.g., imbalance 2) and both sides contain numerals that can give or receive an I.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from a numeral that has only one I, leaving it without any I and making it invalid.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the side that must decrease contains an X and the numeric imbalance is exactly –5, reposition one of the X’s diagonal sticks so that the X becomes a V, decreasing its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is –5 and an X is present on the side that needs to decrease.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal stick from an X and discarding it, leaving a single diagonal that is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign (single horizontal) and an equals sign (two horizontals) are present, you can move one horizontal stick from the equals sign to the minus sign (or vice‑versa), turning '-' into '=' and '=' into '-', while keeping both operators valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both '-' and '=', and the numeric imbalance could be fixed by changing subtraction to equality or the reverse.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=', leaving the equals sign with no sticks, which is not a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: Remove the vertical stick from a plus sign; the remaining horizontal becomes a minus sign, changing addition to subtraction.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '+' and changing addition to subtraction would resolve the numeric imbalance.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' but also removing the horizontal, turning the operator into an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: When relocating a stick from the equality sign, ensure that at least one horizontal stick remains so that the symbol stays a valid operator (either '=' or '-').
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you consider moving a stick from the '=' sign.
matchstick.example: Moving both horizontals from '=', leaving no operator at all.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality when imbalance is 2
matchstick.principle: If the numeric difference between the two sides is exactly 2, move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral on the larger side to a numeral on the smaller side, adjusting both sides by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 2 and both sides contain numerals that can give or receive an I.
matchstick.example: Moving an I from a numeral that cannot lose it without breaking Roman numeral rules.

matchstick.title: Prefer numeral adjustments over operator changes
matchstick.principle: When fixing a matchstick equation, first try transformations that change numeral values (e.g., I transfer, V↔X) before altering operators, because numeral changes preserve the arithmetic structure.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving any mismatch.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' before checking if a V→X conversion could resolve the imbalance.

matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation when moving
matchstick.principle: A stick retains its orientation when relocated; a diagonal stick must remain diagonal, and a vertical stick must remain vertical. Do not attempt to use a diagonal stick as a vertical I (or vice versa).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you move a stick to form a new numeral or operator.
matchstick.example: Using a diagonal stick from a V to form a vertical I, creating an invalid numeral.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any stick can be removed, ignoring that some numerals need all their sticks to stay valid.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that the source numeral will remain a valid Roman numeral after losing the stick; only remove sticks from numerals with surplus sticks (e.g., multiple I's) or use repositioning within the same numeral.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving sticks but neglects the syntactic requirement that the result must be a complete, well‑formed equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After moving a stick, verify that each token (numerals and operators) is still a recognized symbol and that the equation contains exactly one '=', with proper operands on each side.

matchstick.description: Not verifying numeric equality after transformation; resulting equation may be syntactically valid but numerically false
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model stops after finding a plausible visual transformation and forgets to check the arithmetic.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑compute the decimal values of both sides after the move and confirm they match before finalising the answer.

matchstick.description: Moving more than one stick (or removing multiple sticks) violates the single‑stick rule
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes treats a transformation as moving a stick but actually removes two or more sticks (e.g., changing V to X while also taking a stick from elsewhere).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Count the sticks you relocate; ensure exactly one stick is taken from one place and placed elsewhere, with no extra deletions.

matchstick.description: Creating a non‑canonical Roman numeral (e.g., duplicate V, duplicate L, duplicate D, or more than three I's in a row)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may produce a numeral that violates standard Roman numeral conventions because it only tracks stick counts, not ordering rules.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After the move, check the resulting numerals against canonical Roman numeral rules (no repeated V/L/D, max three consecutive I's, proper subtractive notation).
